critical_code_review_comments: The lazy import pattern (`def _chat(): from emergentintegrations.llm.chat import LlmChat, UserMessage; ...`) is now spread across many modules. Consider centralising in a `utils.llm_lazy` helper so a future refactor can't accidentally re-introduce a module-scope import in one file and silently reintroduce the crash-loop.
The existing guard test_no_heavy_llm_imports_at_module_scope in tests/test_no_blocking_imports.py should be run in CI on every PR; recommend adding it as a required check.

For endpoints returning graceful 'AI unavailable' errors when EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is missing, ensure a stable error shape (e.g. `{code:'ai_unavailable'}`) so the frontend can distinguish transient LLM failures from import/config errors.

Covers: health, master-admin test-data candidates+purge (auth + unauth), and a parametrised AI sweep across ai_diagnosis, svc/ai, capex, risk_assessments, equipment predictive-maintenance, admin doc duplicate scan, issues triage. Assertion contract: only 500 with body matching /ImportError|NameError|is not defined|cannot import name|ModuleNotFoundError/i is a failure — every other status (200/400/404/422) is acceptable per task spec.
rca of the issue: Original P0 (recorded in prior iterations): module-scope `from emergentintegrations.llm.chat import LlmChat` transitively imported litellm at boot, which in the egress-restricted prod container blocked uvicorn from binding :8001 → k8s readiness probe timed out → crash-loop. Fix (this iteration verifies): all such imports moved to function-local scope (or TYPE_CHECKING for annotations). Verification approach: hit each touched endpoint through the real ingress; any 500 whose body indicated import/NameError would prove a regression. None observed.
